reasoning: Upper bound: any line of the grid has 5 rows, each row is a line, so a set with no three collinear has at most 2 points per row, giving at most 2*5 = 10 points. Construction achieving 10: {(1,0),(3,0),(1,1),(4,1),(0,2),(4,2),(0,3),(2,3),(2,4),(3,4)}. It has exactly two points in each row and each column. Verified no three collinear by checking, for every direction (dx,dy) with dx,dy in {1..4} coprime and both signs (slopes ±1, ±2, ±1/2, ±3, ±1/3, ±4, ±1/4, ±3/2, ±2/3, ±4/3, ±3/4), the invariant dy*x - dx*y: e.g. x-y gives 1,3,0,3,-2,2,-3,-1,-2,-1; x+y gives 1,3,2,5,2,6,3,5,6,7; 2x-y gives 2,6,1,7,-2,6,-3,1,0,2; 2x+y gives 2,6,3,9,2,10,3,7,8,10; x-2y gives 1,3,-1,2,-4,0,-6,-4,-6,-5; x+2y gives 1,3,3,6,4,8,6,8,10,11; and similarly for the remaining slopes; every value occurs at most twice, so no three points share a line. Hence the maximum is 10.
